Thursday was a broad down day for Jaleel's book, with only AstraZeneca (+1.72%), Expand Energy (+0.26%), On Holding (+0.04%), and Neurocrine Biosciences (+0.92%) managing any green. The heaviest damage came from Boston Scientific, which shed another 4.14% — the largest single-day drag — compounding a position already sitting at a –12.1% unrealized loss under an elevated guidance-cut flag. NVIDIA fell 2.37%, ADBE fell 2.37%, and LULU dropped 2.85%, adding to what are already the book's deepest underwater names (LULU at –24.2%, RKLB at –20.9%). ABT, the largest single weight at 10.5%, gave back 1.78% despite still sitting on a healthy +19.5% gain. The macro backdrop explained much of the software weakness: geopolitical tensions and renewed inflation fears drove rotation out of growth stocks, pressuring ADBE and peers, even as SAP's headline pointed to mixed software sentiment on the day.

The drift problem is concentrated in three names. BSX carries an elevated flag — guidance slashed to 7–8.5% growth, flat through Q3 guided — yet still carries a Strong Buy verdict; price and thesis are clearly pulling apart, with the next catalyst not until October 28. LULU is a similar story: five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, tariff margin pressure, China stalled, and a guide cut in June, yet the model rates it Strong Buy — that conviction needs to be stress-tested, not accepted at face value. RKLB is the outlier in a different direction: rated AVOID with a QARP score of 39.5 (the weakest in the book by a wide margin), –20.9% in the hole, and still carrying a 6.5% weight. There is no constructive thesis visible in the data to justify that weight at that rating.

Watch ADBE closely — its earnings call falls today (Sep 10 next-event flag), and the headline risk around AI-moat fears and CFO departure means the narrative, not just the numbers, could move the stock sharply. The SPGI headline around OpenAI's ChatGPT for Financial Services integrating with S&P Global is a genuine strategic development worth monitoring for whether it adds to or complicates SPGI's moat. AZN's +1.72% was a rare bright spot and its Strong Buy rating with QARP of 74.1 looks defensively sound; it is one of the few positions behaving in line with thesis.

attention.headline: Guidance slashed, –12.1% loss, and another 4.14% drop today — thesis-price gap is widening
attention.note: FY26 growth cut to 7–8.5% with flat guidance through Q3, yet the position remains rated Strong Buy and carries an 8.7% weight; with the next catalyst not until Oct 28, Jaleel needs to decide whether to reduce exposure now or explicitly accept the drawdown risk through earnings.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated name at 6.5% weight, –20.9% unrealized loss — no constructive case in the data
attention.note: RKLB is the only AVOID in the book, carries the lowest QARP score (39.5) by a significant margin, and is the third-deepest underwater position; a 6.5% weight in a name the model explicitly flags to avoid is a direct conflict that needs a resolution, not monitoring.

attention.headline: Earnings event flagged for today (Sep 10) — AI-moat narrative risk is live
attention.note: The risk flag notes that the last print (beat-and-raise) still sold off due to narrative fears around Claude Design and CFO exit; today's report could reprice the stock sharply in either direction regardless of the underlying numbers, and the position needs a pre-earnings stance.

attention.headline: –24.2% loss, five straight negative comps, guidance cut — Strong Buy verdict needs a challenge
attention.note: Americas comps –5% for a fifth consecutive quarter, tariffs gutting margins, and China stalled; the Strong Buy rating with a next catalyst not until Dec 9 means Jaleel is carrying a significant underwater weight through a long information vacuum with deteriorating fundamentals.
